$comment: The recorded state of the `endora new storefront` acceptance criterion
(specs/071-modular-packaging/roadmap.md § F7). `acceptance:storefront-scaffold:ci`
compares a run to this file and fails on drift in EITHER direction: a newly-red
assertion fails, and so does a newly-green one nobody recorded. An unrecorded pass
is a criterion whose meaning moved without anybody reading it.
It landed all-green, which is unusual for an acceptance file in this repository and
is the finding rather than a formality: `acceptance:package-schema` landed red on
seven of nine because the capability it measures did not exist yet, and this one
measures a capability that turned out to be one manifest line short of working.
The roadmap named this criterion as the half that `could not be sized without
trying it` — whether a scaffolded storefront builds from packed tarballs depends on
how much of the packages' `exports` maps and `use client` boundaries survive an
install that is not a workspace link. Measured: all of it. The one thing that did
not survive was the reference storefront's own manifest, which declared none of the
eight `@tiptap/*` packages its build resolves from the workspace root.
A6 is `pass` because the job boots a backend for it. A run with no
PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL records `unmeasured` instead — never a pass — because a boot
with no backend measures the storefront's error page rather than the storefront.
If this job ever stops booting one, A6 drifts to `unmeasured` and fails, which is
the direction that keeps the headline claim honest.
SINCE 2026-09-06 A6 IS TWO BOOTS AND ITS `pass` MEANS MORE THAN IT DID. The state
is unchanged and the claim behind it is not: the run now points the instance at the
backend through the variables the instance's own `.env.example` declares, and then
boots it a second time with those same variables aimed at an address nothing listens
on. A pass needs the first boot below 500 and the second at or above it. Until this
landed the harness exported `PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` — the *backend's* variable, for the
public origin its gateway callbacks need, and one no file in the storefront has ever
read — so the instance fell back to the `http://localhost:3001` its fetchers compile
in. A6 was therefore green whenever the run's backend happened to sit on that address
and red whenever it sat anywhere else, in both cases for a reason belonging to the
harness rather than to the criterion. The probe is what stops the green meaning `the
fallback answered`: a second boot whose configuration reaches nothing has to fail, or
the first answer proves nothing and the assertion is `unmeasured`.
SINCE 2026-09-04 THE RECORD IS PER SUPPLY ROUTE (feature 104, § 1.6). The six
assertions are the same under both; what differs is how the instance got its
`@endora-commerce/*` packages, and `A3 pass` therefore means two different things.
`tarball` packs them out of this checkout and pins them through `pnpm.overrides`;
`registry` installs the semver ranges the scaffold wrote, from a real registry,
through the `.npmrc` `endora new storefront --registry` emits. The mode is chosen
by ENDORA_NPM_REGISTRY in the environment, so a run with no registry variables —
every local run, and the CI job as it stands — takes the tarball route.
`registry` is recorded `unrun`, and that is a state rather than a placeholder. No
version of the three packages is on the rehearsal registry: `version:packages`
(§ 1.7) has not run, every manifest still reads `0.0.0`, and the scaffold writes its
ranges from those manifests — so a run of that mode today would fail A3 for a reason
that says nothing about the criterion. Recording six predicted states instead would
be the one thing this file exists to refuse. The first real run of the mode drifts,
naming every assertion it measured, and the record arrives from that run.

registry.why: The three packages are unpublished at the versions the scaffold writes (all `0.0.0`), so this route cannot be measured until feature 104 § 1.7 has cut and published a version. Its states are recorded by the first run of it, never predicted here.

history.what: A6 gained a discrimination probe, and the harness started configuring the instance with the variables the instance declares
history.detail: The six states are unchanged. `boot()` set PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL, which is the backend's own variable and which the storefront reads nowhere, so every A6 measured the compiled-in `http://localhost:3001` fallback: 200 when the run's backend sat there, 500 when it sat anywhere else. Measured on master at http://127.0.0.1:3101 — `A6 FAIL ... answered / with 500` — against a scaffolded instance that serves 200 the moment BACKEND_BASE_URL names the same backend. The names now come off the instance's own `.env.example` through the derivation `endora new storefront` prints in its next steps, they reach `next build` as well as `next start` because Next inlines a NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable at build time, and a second boot against an address nothing listens on has to fail before the first is read as a pass.

history.what: the criterion landed with the command (F7 scaffold half), all six green
history.detail: A1 the copy names nothing above its own directory; A2 no `workspace:` range survives; A3 `pnpm install` outside the checkout from three packed tarballs, pinned through `pnpm.overrides` because page-builder-core's own dependency on contracts is equally unpublished; A4 every @endora-commerce/* package resolves outside the checkout; A5 `next build`; A6 `next start` answered / with 200 against a running backend.

history.what: the record became per supply route; `tarball` keeps its six measured states, `registry` arrives unrun
history.detail: Feature 104 § 1.6. The criterion gained a second mode that installs from a registry rather than from packed tarballs, selected by ENDORA_NPM_REGISTRY. The tarball mode is unchanged in every respect — same six assertions, same states, still the default — and its block is the previous `assertions` object moved under it. Nothing about the two-way drift rule changed; what changed is which block a run is compared against.
